title: WPMS/1151/2013 of Smt. Vijay Laxmi Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No.1151 of 2013 (M/S)

State of Uttarakhand & Ors. ....Respondents
Mr. V.K. Kohli, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Kanti Ram Sharma, Advocate for the
petitioner
Mr. Devesh Ghildiyal, Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand/respondent no.1
and 2
Mr. Rahul Consul, Advocate for respondent no.3
Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate for the respondent no.4
With
Writ Petition No.1850 of 2013 (M/S)
Faquir Chand ......Petitioner
versus

State of Uttarakhand & Ors. ....Respondents
Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate for the petitioner
Mr. Devesh Ghildiyal, Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand/respondent no.1
and 2
Mr. Rahul Consul, Advocate for respondent no.3
Mr. V.K. Kohli, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Kanti Ram Sharma, Advocate for
respondent no.4
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Lok Pal Singh, J.

Since the controversy involved in both these
writ petitions is same, hence, for the sake of brevity and
convenience, these writ petitions are being disposed of
by this common judgment.
2. By means of WPMS No.1151 of 2013,
petitioner Smt. Vijay Laxmi has sought quashing of
order dated 02.04.2013 passed by respondent no.2 in
revision no.332 of 2013.

2
3. By means of Writ Petition (S/S) No.1850 of
2013, petitioner Faquir Chand has sought quashing of
part of order dated 2.4.2013 passed by Additional
Secretary, Awas in revision no.332 of 2013, to the extent
whereby the learned Additional Secretary has permitted
compounding of the construction within 165 sq.ft.

4. Facts necessary for proper adjudication of the
case are that Smt. Vijay Laxmi (petitioner herein)
purchased a shop bearing no.163, situated at Chakrata
Road, Dehradun through registered sale deed dated
16.05.1991 from Smt. Hemlata Sharma and Smt.
Shakuntala. As the construction of the shop/kiosk was
very old and roof of the shop was badly damaged,
petitioner moved an application before the third
respondent- MDDA for reconstruction of the roof. Vide
order dated 19.8.1991, sanction was granted to the
petitioner to construct the roof on the condition that
except replacement of roof, no other construction will be
carried out by the petitioner and that on road widening
the petitioner will herself demolish the construction
affected by road widening. Pursuant to the sanction,
petitioner started replacement of roof but while the
repair work was underway, the western side wall of the
shop got damaged and fallen down; subsequently the
petitioner started reconstruction of the wall, including
some excess area. Fourth respondent, who was a tenant
in the adjoining shop, made a complaint to Chairman,
MDDA. On the complaint so made, a show cause notice
dated 17.9.1991 was issued to the petitioner Smt. Vijay
Laxmi, calling her explanation as to why construction
raised by her, be not demolished. Petitioner submitted
her reply to the show cause notice. A spot inspection

3
was got conducted by the third respondent and
thereafter the third respondent, vide order/letter dated
28.1.1992, permitted compounding on deposit of
compounding fee. Fourth respondent felt aggrieved with
the compounding order, preferred a revision before the
State Government. The Secretary, Avas, vide order dated
06.11.1992, allowed the revision and quashed the order
dated 28.1.1992.
5. Feeling aggrieved, petitioner Smt. Vijay Laxmi
preferred a writ petition before this Court being WPMS
No.2729 of 2012, assailing the order dated 06.11.1992.
This Court allowed the revision on the ground that the
order dated 06.11.1992 was an ex-parte order and
remanded back the matter to the Secretary to decide the
revision afresh, after providing opportunity of hearing to
the petitioner Smt. Vijay Laxmi. After remand, second
respondent partly allowed the revision and set aside the
orders dated 04.01.1992, 10.01.1992 and 28.01.1992
and provided an opportunity to the petitioner Smt. Vijay
Laxmi to make alterations in the newly constructed
shop so as to make the area of the shop as 165.00
Sq.ft., within two months.
6. Mr. V.K. Kohli, learned Senior Counsel
appearing for the petitioner Smt. Vijay Laxmi would
submit that originally sanction was granted to the
petitioner by order dated 4.1.1992 to repair roof of the
shop but during the course of repair work, as one side
of wall was fallen down, the petitioner raised
construction including some excess area. He would
further submit that after the complaint made by
respondent no.4, a compounding application was filed

4
by the petitioner, which was allowed by third
respondent on payment of compounding fee, which was
well within the domain of the MDDA. He would further
submit that as the compounding fee was deposited by
the petitioner in compliance of order dated 28.01.1992
the second respondent has committed illegality in
setting aside the orders dated 4.1.1992, 10.1.1992 and
28.1.1992. Learned Senior Counsel would submit that
the second respondent has partly allowed the revision,
without assigning any reason, except taking into
consideration the master plan. It is contended that the
master plan ought not to have been taken into
consideration as the petitioner has submitted an
undertaking to the effect that if in future there will be
road widening and it is affected by the construction, the
petitioner shall herself remove the construction and will
not claim any right in regard to the constructed area.
7. On the other hand, Mr. Piyush Garg, learned
counsel for appearing for fourth respondent/petitioner
Faquir Chand would submit that originally the area of
the shop/kiosk was 165 sq.ft. which was increased upto
202.92 by the petitioner Smt. Vijay Laxmi, under the
garb of changing the roof. It is contended that as per the
master plan, the width of Chakrata Road is mentioned
to be 45 metres and as such no construction within
22.5 metres from the centre of Chakrata Road is
permissible and thus the same cannot be compounded
also. It is contended that the third respondent has
illegally permitted compounding of construction.
8. Having considered the submissions of learned
counsel for the parties and on perusal of entire material

5
available on record, it would reveal that an old shop
measuring 165 sq.ft., with open piece of land, was
purchased by the petitioner Smt. Vijay Laxmi. She was
permitted to change the roof of the shop but during
renovation as one side of wall was fallen, petitioner
started re-constructing the wall, thus, after inclusion of
the area of the walls of the shop, it came to 202.92 sq.ft.
Petitioner applied for compounding when a notice was
issued to her on the complaint made by fourth
respondent. Compounding application was allowed and
the excess construction was compounded on depositing
the compounding fee.
9. Admittedly, petitioner Smt. Vijay Laxmi has
deposited the compounding fee. She has also submitted
an undertaking before the Secretary, MDDA, Dehradun
to the effect that if in future there will be road widening
and if it is affected by the construction, the petitioner
shall herself remove the construction and will not claim
any right in regard to the constructed area. It appears to
this Court that the second respondent while passing the
impugned order has not taken into consideration that
the construction has been compounded by charging
compounding fee. There was no justification on the part
of second respondent to interfere in the order of third
respondent after the compounding fee was charged from
the petitioner. The revisional jurisdiction cannot be
considered like an original jurisdiction. In the case at
hand, the second respondent has acted like an original
authority and has exceeded in exercising the revisional
jurisdiction and has illegally interfered with the orders
passed by third respondent. Impugned order dated
02.04.2013 is, therefore, liable to be set aside.

6
10. In view of the aforesaid discussion, impugned
order dated 2.4.2013 is hereby quashed and set aside.
WPMS No.1151 of 2013 is allowed. Consequently,
WPMS No.1850 of 2013 stands dismissed.
11. No order as to costs.
 (Lok Pal Singh, J.)
 27.02.2019
 Rajni
